verdict.root_cause: shippingservice is running the wrong container artifact. An automated image-reference update landed on shippingservice at 14:39:44Z — about three minutes before the 14:42:45 onset — pointing it at an adservice-tagged demo image, and unlike the three preceding apply/revert cycles this one was never reverted, so it was the only change in effect anywhere in the investigated blast radius at onset [tr_412929c4514d]. A shippingservice pod running the adservice binary cannot serve the shipping RPCs (GetQuote/ShipOrder), which explains why shippingservice and its quote dependency alerted together and why downstream order-side consumers (accounting, email, frauddetection) alerted three minutes later, while checkoutservice — which alerted first merely because it is the caller that notices — shows no aggregate error-rate regression and continues logging accepted PlaceOrder calls [tr_3a6d36c988e6, tr_2f526671f154]. Nothing was changed on checkoutservice or productcatalogservice in the window [tr_efbc29cfaecc, tr_8760e94b17eb], and every cartservice mutation had been reverted ~1.9h before onset [tr_c1d1e350769a].
verdict.reasoning: The classification rests on mechanism, not on the fact that a change record exists: the artifact now running as shippingservice is not the shippingservice artifact, which is the definition of bad_deploy, and the remedy is to restore the correct image reference (rollback) rather than to tune any value. Timing and persistence are what elevate this change above the others: it landed 3 minutes pre-onset and was still in effect at onset, whereas the shippingservice quote-endpoint override closed 13 minutes before onset and the entire cartservice apply/revert set closed ~1.9 hours before onset [tr_412929c4514d, tr_c1d1e350769a]. The direction of blame is away from the alerting service: checkoutservice's error ratio is statistically indistinguishable from baseline with unchanged range and lower variance, its only change point is a window-boundary artifact, and its logs show uninterrupted info-level order acceptance through 14:47:32 with no downstream connection errors and no restart [tr_3a6d36c988e6, tr_2f526671f154] — a profile consistent with a service that noticed a partner failing, not one that is failing itself. The two other services whose change logs were pulled are clean at onset [tr_efbc29cfaecc, tr_8760e94b17eb]. Confidence is held at medium because the shippingservice hypothesis is supported entirely by change-record inference; no shippingservice metric, log, or trace evidence was gathered to show it actually failing.
open_questions: No metrics, logs, or traces were collected for shippingservice at all — the wrong-image hypothesis is inferred from the change record and has not been confirmed by observed shippingservice errors, crash-loops, or missing RPC handlers.

The three earlier cycles applied the same anomalous image reference and were reverted; it is unsettled whether those earlier applications produced the same symptom signature (which would confirm causality) or passed unnoticed.

checkoutservice's aggregate error ratio did not move, so the actual user-visible symptom that fired the 14:42:45 critical alert is unexplained; the metric query returned no per-RPC-method, per-downstream-target, latency, or request-rate breakdown [tr_3a6d36c988e6].
The checkoutservice log result was truncated across 12:43:28–14:45:17, so the onset interval itself (14:40–14:45) was never observed [tr_2f526671f154].

Why accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice, and quoteservice all alerted at exactly 14:45:45 is untested — a shared alert evaluation interval, a Kafka order-pipeline stall, or a common cause upstream of all of them remain distinguishable only with data not gathered.
5 unmeasured edges in the triage graph were never crossed; a cause outside the six services queried is not excluded.
The productcatalogservice change query looked only forward from onset, so a pre-existing change still in effect there would not appear [tr_8760e94b17eb].

alternatives.root_cause: The shippingservice QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR override that pointed quote lookups at a non-existent host left lingering effects (stale connection pools, retry backlog, saturated request queues) that surfaced as failures after the config itself was reverted.
alternatives.why_not: The override was reverted at 14:29:07Z, 13 minutes before onset, so it was not in effect when the incident started; this requires an unobserved lingering-state mechanism, whereas the image change was still live at onset [tr_412929c4514d].

alternatives.root_cause: The incident originates in a service never examined — one of the 5 unmeasured edges or another order-path dependency — and the shippingservice image update is a coincidental automation artifact from a recurring fault-injection harness.
alternatives.why_not: It is unfalsified only because those edges were never queried, and it has to treat a three-minute pre-onset, still-in-effect wrong-artifact change as coincidence; it names no mechanism and no fix.

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying shippingservice at its pre-14:39:44Z image should restore a real shipping binary behind GetQuote/ShipOrder. Observable as shippingservice's error ratio in calls_total returning to pre-14:39 baseline and its alert clearing, quoteservice's alert clearing, and the accounting/email/frauddetection alerts clearing within one or two evaluation intervals. Capture one shippingservice metric and log query before acting: no shippingservice telemetry exists in this investigation, so without a pre-state there is nothing to compare against.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if shippingservice error ratio stays elevated after the recreate, or the quote/order-side alerts do not clear within two evaluation intervals. Also falsified if the pre-rollback capture shows shippingservice serving shipping RPCs normally on the adservice-tagged image — consistent with checkoutservice's flat aggregate error ratio [tr_3a6d36c988e6] — meaning the mechanism is wrong. Recurrence via the same automation cycle would show this treated a harness artifact.
proposal.risk: Medium confidence resting only on a change record; no observed shippingservice errors or crash-loops. If the diagnosis is wrong, this recreates a container central to the order path, adds a fresh in-flight failure window during a live incident, and destroys the process state needed to confirm the hypothesis. If the recorded prior image is not the canonical shipping artifact, the rollback lands on a second wrong image.
proposal.blast_radius: shippingservice alone during the recreate. Its caller checkoutservice (and frontend behind it) sees connection resets on shipping RPCs; quoteservice sees shipping traffic pause then resume; order-side consumers accounting, email, and frauddetection see a brief further gap before recovery.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Checkout alerts first, then its downstream consumers fan out three minutes later — a real multi-service failure centered on checkout, not dismissible. No open incidents to attribute it to, and nothing in the alert pattern yet distinguishes a deploy, config, or dependency cause.
